# InvestingNoobs

> InvestingNoobs is a free, browser-based learning hub for cryptocurrency, investing and trading. It combines a live market tracker with InvestingNoobs Academy: 50 practical lessons that move from market vocabulary to research, execution, DeFi, prop-firm risk, portfolio construction, security and long-term habits.

## Start here

- [Free crypto and trading course](https://investingnoobs.com/blog.html): the 50-lesson roadmap and progress tracker.
- [Full course index](https://investingnoobs.com/llms-full.txt): every lesson title and direct article URL.
- [Lesson 1: What is a cryptocurrency?](https://investingnoobs.com/article.html?id=l1): beginner starting point.
- [Lesson 19: What is a prop firm?](https://investingnoobs.com/article.html?id=l19): evaluation rules, fees and risk.
- [Lesson 50: How to build a long-term investing routine](https://investingnoobs.com/article.html?id=l50): final process chapter.
- [50-question final assessment](https://investingnoobs.com/test.html): one practical question for each lesson; 80% required to pass.
- [Investor Passport](https://investingnoobs.com/passport.html): choose a starting level and goal to receive a personalised three-step route through the course and practice tools.
- [Research Room](https://investingnoobs.com/research.html): build an evidence-based thesis for a crypto, stock or commodity with a practical checklist.
- [Decision Lab](https://investingnoobs.com/decisionlab.html): build a virtual allocation and practise five risk-management decisions with transparent feedback.
- [Portfolio Blueprint](https://investingnoobs.com/portfolio.html): turn an allocation idea into an explainable, risk-first practice blueprint with concentration and fee checks.
- [Live market tracker](https://investingnoobs.com/): crypto, stocks and commodity reference prices.

## What the course teaches

Cryptocurrency, Bitcoin, Ethereum, blockchain, exchanges, wallets, stablecoins, market capitalisation, inflation, volatility, fees, stocks, commodities, diversification, technical analysis, fundamental analysis, order types, leverage, margin, stop-losses, drawdown, prop firms, trading psychology, DeFi, smart contracts, DAOs, bridges, liquidity pools, yield farming, portfolio rebalancing, crypto records, phishing and rug-pull risk.

## Editorial principles

The lessons are written in plain English with definitions, worked examples, checklists, exercises and further reading. They are educational, not personal financial, legal or tax advice. No page promises profits or guarantees that a strategy will work. Verify current market data, regulation, fees and tax treatment with authoritative sources before acting.
